open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict creation on resubmission
open_points.text: “recorded once and then reused, never computed again” contradicts “Computed by the kernel when an implementation is submitted” and “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time”; M09 also permits activation from a submission “new or reused.”
open_points.question: When an equal implementation is submitted again while the corpus digest is unchanged, does the kernel reuse the existing AdmissionVerdict and its TrialExecutions, or run the corpus again and create fresh admission evidence?
options: Reuse the single existing verdict and perform no trial executions
Run every case again and replace or add admission evidence
Run every case again only for observation but retain the original verdict
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the existing verdict without executing the corpus again.

witness.initial: Implementation I has an admitted verdict for corpus digest C and is not currently active.
events: An authoring agent submits code equal to I while the active corpus still has digest C.
outcomes: The kernel reuses the recorded verdict, runs no trial cases, and activates I.
The kernel runs every case again at admission time and bases activation on the new executions.
witness.observer: The submitting agent sees new TrialExecution evidence or its absence and may see a different activation result.

open_points.subject: Determinism of admission for functions using undetected time or randomness
open_points.text: K-02 says code obtaining time or chance by another way “is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other,” while K-05 says “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” and M08 makes that verdict permanently reusable for the implementation and corpus digest.
open_points.question: What does “deterministic verdict” mean when the admitted implementation may obtain time or randomness through an undetected route and therefore produce different outputs for the same trial case?
options: The first admission observations determine a permanent cached verdict even if another execution would differ
Such an implementation is ineligible because any dependency on time or chance violates function purity
The verdict must be recomputed or otherwise invalidated when later executions disagree
open_points.default_guess: Judge the first admission executions normally and permanently reuse their recorded verdict for that implementation and corpus digest.

witness.initial: A contract has one case expecting output 0; an implementation obtains a changing clock or random bit without using the blocked standard-library entry points and returns that bit.
events: The agent submits the implementation when it returns 0.
The same implementation and unchanged corpus are considered again when it would return 1.
outcomes: The first execution admits the implementation and the one recorded verdict remains admitted.
Admission is not treated as a stable deterministic fact because the same implementation and corpus can fail, so it is rejected or reconsidered.
witness.observer: The agent and runs using the contract observe whether the implementation is active and whether later output 1 is possible.
